title: Leasing and tenancy boundaries
audience: Home-based property managers who may be asked to take on leasing or tenancy tasks
learningOutcomes: Identify the leasing and tenancy tasks that are outside the scope of this course.
Describe why the licence position for leasing must be confirmed before any leasing task is accepted.
Refer leasing and tenancy questions and record the referral.

instruction.heading: Leasing is not a maintenance task
instruction.body: Leasing covers finding and screening tenants, negotiating and signing tenancy agreements, collecting rent and managing bonds and notices. These tasks are not part of property maintenance. In many places they are regulated, and the regulated status differs by state and territory. Official pages checked in this pass confirm the position in New South Wales and set a narrower scope in Queensland. Until the position is confirmed for the property's state, a property manager partner must not accept leasing work, and must not represent that they are licensed to do it.

instruction.heading: Refer and record
instruction.body: When an owner or a tenant asks for a leasing or tenancy task, record the request, state that the position is being confirmed, and refer it to the owner and to the relevant state authority or licensed agent. Do not give tenancy advice. Keep the maintenance and condition work separate, because it can continue under the owner's instructions while the leasing question is resolved. NSW's guidance separates administrative and receipting tasks from agent functions: a worker who only issues keys to existing tenants and collects rent from them under the manager's direction does not need the licence for those tasks, provided they do not carry out agent functions (page last modified 22 September 2025).

procedure: Identify whether the request is a leasing or tenancy task, or a maintenance task.
For a leasing or tenancy task, stop and record the request.
Confirm the licence position for leasing in the property's state before accepting any leasing work.
Refer the request to the owner and to the relevant state authority or licensed agent.
Keep maintenance and condition work separate, and continue it only under the owner's written instruction.
Record the referral and the date.

workedExamples.situation: A tenant asks you to find a new tenant for a vacant unit and to hold the deposit until the new tenancy starts.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should you accept this as part of the portfolio service?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Finding tenants and holding a deposit are leasing and trust-handling tasks. In New South Wales, leasing and bond collection sit inside the licence scope, so the worker must not do them without that licence. Queensland and Victoria positions must be checked before any such work. Refer the request to the owner and the relevant state authority, record it, and continue only the maintenance work the owner has instructed.

equipmentAndPpe: Contact list for the relevant state authority

commonErrors.error: Accepting leasing work because the owner asked.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the licence position for the state before accepting, and refer.

commonErrors.error: Holding a deposit or collecting rent without confirmed rules.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not handle deposits or rent until the state rules are confirmed.

commonErrors.error: Representing that the worker is licensed for leasing.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the worker's position accurately and refer leasing work.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Leasing licence position by state. New South Wales: the licence for real estate agents covers leasing and property management, including a restricted class for on-site residential letting (page last modified 20 October 2026). Queensland: a current resident letting agent licence is needed for that work, and the page links it to units in multi-unit complexes for owners and strata bodies (page last updated 26 October 2026). Confirm the state position before accepting any leasing work.

Bonds and deposits: state law caps the bond and requires it to be lodged with a state authority rather than held privately. NSW caps a bond at four weeks' rent, and the bond is paid to NSW Fair Trading, which issues the receipt (page last modified 16 September 2026). Queensland caps it at four weeks' rent and requires lodgement with the RTA within 10 days by the owner or manager (no page date shown). Victoria caps it at one month's rent and requires payment to the RTBA inside ten working days of receipt (page last updated 8 December 2025). Do not hold or handle a deposit until the state rules and the licence position are confirmed.
Completing this lesson does not give a real estate licence, a leasing authority or any right to hold or handle tenant money.

qualityStandard: No leasing task is accepted before the state licence position is confirmed and recorded.
Every leasing or tenancy request is recorded and referred.
No representation of licensed status is made without confirmation.
documentationEvidence: Referral record for each leasing or tenancy request
Record of the state licence position check and its source
Owner's written instruction for any maintenance work continuing
summary: Leasing and tenancy are not maintenance tasks.
Stop, record and refer leasing and tenancy requests.
Keep maintenance and condition work separate and under the owner's written instruction.

knowledgeChecks.question: A tenant asks you to find a new tenant and hold the deposit. What is correct?
options: Accept it as part of the portfolio service the owner already pays for each month in full
Record the request, confirm the leasing and deposit positions for the state, and refer it
Hold the deposit until a tenant is found, since the funds are safe with you in the office
Ask the tenant to pay you directly, since it saves time for both of you on the job

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the status of the leasing licence position in this course?
options: Confirmed as not required in every state, so no check is needed for any property and no state record is needed for the file or the owner's records
Confirmed as covered by the handyman licence held by the property manager on staff, so the state check can be skipped for the whole portfolio
Confirmed for some states and not others, so the position must be checked for the property's state before leasing work is accepted
Confirmed as required only in Victoria, so other states need no check at all for any property in the portfolio
